title: Just So You Know
text: Did I want it to notice? Honestly, yeah. Some part of me wanted to wake up and feel the difference, wanted the morning to be heavier than usual, wanted something to confirm that what we had actually had weight. But it didn’t. Same time. Same silence. Same everything. And that was almost worse than if it had hurt loudly. Quiet indifference is a strange thing to sit with when you’re the one who actually felt something. I’m not complaining. Just being honest with you for once without dressing it up.

title: This Is What Quiet Looks Like
text: Three days. No noise. I didn’t fill it with anything desperate or distracting, just let the silence be what it was and worked through it the way I work through most things. Slowly. Privately. My phone existed somewhere in the room and I just didn’t prioritize it. Not discipline. Not strategy. Just genuinely had other things to tend to. What surprised me was how quickly the quiet stopped feeling like absence and started feeling like mine again. Like I’d reclaimed something I didn’t know I’d been lending out. That part I wasn’t expecting.

title: I Actually Like Who I’m Becoming
text: I looked in the mirror two days ago. Not in a vain way, just kind of checked in. And I genuinely liked what I saw. Not just the body, although yeah, the body too. More the expression. Something is settling in me that wasn’t there before. Quieter. More certain. And then I remembered that you and Nuzu actually made something for me once. I’m someone who buys his own everything, always have been, so I don’t usually have a category for that kind of gesture. But that one got its own category. Quietly. Without announcement.

title: What We Could Have Been
text: I sent you that text. You know the one. I was mostly talking about myself if I’m being honest, classic, but somewhere in the middle of all that I said something that made you laugh. And I heard it. And I laughed too, which I wasn’t expecting, and for like two seconds the whole thing felt stupidly easy. Natural. Like something that didn’t need to be constructed. I think about that laugh sometimes. Not obsessively. Just the way you think about a song you heard once in a place you can’t go back to.

title: The Me You Actually Got
text: You didn’t get a version I’d rehearsed. Some people get the edited one, the one that shows up correctly and says the right things at the right volume. You got the one that actually existed between the edits. And you used to send me voice notes. Covering songs. My songs specifically, the ones I actually love, in your own voice, completely unprompted. I never told you what that did. I should have. There’s something about hearing a person you like wrap their voice around something you love that quietly destroys the part of you that was trying to stay unbothered. I was unbothered until those.

title: I Told You Something
text: I didn’t tell you anything. That’s what makes it sit so strange. You found it yourself, somewhere in the middle of going through my numbers, a fake account wearing my name that I had nothing to do with. And instead of coming to me first, instead of asking me directly, you took it somewhere else. To someone else. That’s the part I keep returning to. Not the finding. The direction you walked in after. And when I found out there was this sudden electric thing in my stomach, sharp, like missing a step in complete darkness. I’ve been misread before. In rooms I still have to sit in. I hate it more than I know how to say.

title: The Moment I Knew
text: It was never about the cost. I need to say that clearly because if you think it was about money you’ve missed the entire thing. I’ve always taken care of myself. Always. What I wanted, what I’ve actually always wanted, is to feel remembered through someone’s actions. Not words. Actions. The tragedy isn’t what happened. The tragedy is being looked at constantly but never actually looked into. Seen but not known. That’s a specific kind of loneliness and it’s one I’m very familiar with and I was starting to think maybe, maybe that was changing.

title: You Talked
text: I don’t need to be loud about this. You talked. And it got somewhere it had no business being. Someone I actually respect heard something about me that wasn’t true, built on something I never consented to share, wearing my name on it like it fit. And even now, even knowing it’s been addressed, some part of me sits with this quiet thing I can’t fully shake. Not paranoia. Just this honest awareness that some people will look at me differently. Even if the record is corrected. Even if everyone moves on. Rumours leave a residue. That part I haven’t fully made peace with yet.

title: Five Days
text: Five days. And somewhere in the middle of day three I had a moment. Not a dramatic one. Just quiet and heavy and honest. I was sorry I made her cry. That sat with me more than I expected it to. I was sorry I couldn’t open up the way I probably should have, the way she probably needed me to. You can look at a flower every single day and appreciate it completely and still never once ask it how it’s been. I think I did that. I think I was doing that. And I was sorry. Genuinely. That part wasn’t performance.

title: What I Did With The Time
text: It was a random thought on a random day, genuinely, I just looked at my screen and felt like putting it down for a while. So I did. Deactivated. No countdown, no statement, just a decision made in about four seconds because that’s how I make most decisions when they’re actually mine. Worked. Ate properly. Took care of myself the way I always do when nobody’s watching. It was supposed to be maybe three days. I wasn’t counting. What I didn’t know was what was unraveling on the other side of that silence. The 2am texts. The spiral. I found out later and my first feeling honestly wasn’t what you’d expect. It was just. Tired.

title: Some People Don’t Get Access
text: Most people get the edited version of me. Polished. Appropriate. Easy to be around. That’s not dishonesty, that’s just how I move through the world when I don’t fully trust the container. But occasionally, rarely, I make a decision about someone. A quiet internal decision that most people never even know is happening. And I open something. Not everything. Just enough that it’s real. You were inside that decision. I was actively choosing you. I don’t know if you understood what that meant at the time. I don’t know if you understand it now.

title: That One Hour
text: There’s a specific hour of my day that started feeling different because of you. I’m not going to tell you which one. That’s mine to keep. But I noticed it. And when things went the way they went I noticed its absence the way you notice a sound that’s been in the background for so long that the silence it leaves is louder than the sound ever was. I’ve filled it now. It’s handled. I’m fine. But I clocked the vacancy. Sat with it for exactly as long as it deserved. That’s the only receipt you get.

title: Don’t Confuse This
text: I want to be careful here because I don’t want you reading this wrong. Me still being here is not confusion. It’s not habit. It’s not me not knowing what happened because I know exactly what happened and I’ve sat with every part of it. I’m here because I made a choice. And part of that choice, if I’m being real with you in the language we actually speak, is that somewhere underneath all of it I love you. Not loudly. Not as an announcement. Just as a quiet fact that kept showing up every time I tried to argue myself out of this. I’m still here. That’s what that means.

title: You Have No Idea
text: You got a glimpse of something most people apply for and don’t receive. Not the surface version, not the guy who looks good and trains hard and keeps his peace, you had a window into something quieter and more specific than that. The version that actually thinks about people. That replays conversations. That notices small things and doesn’t always say so. You saw maybe ten percent of that and I think it moved you. I think you knew it was rare even if you couldn’t name it. Ten percent. Imagine the rest.

title: Three Days
text: I went offline because I felt like it. That’s the whole reason. No deeper strategy, no statement, just a man who saw people improving themselves on a screen and thought, let me actually do that instead of watching it. Deactivated on a whim. Worked. Slept clean. Trained. Read. I was genuinely, completely fine. Meanwhile I’m finding out later that there were 2am texts, spiraling, accounts being deactivated, gaslighting dressed up as love. “If I didn’t love you I wouldn’t have done this.” I read that and I just felt tired. Because love doesn’t need that sentence. It just doesn’t.

title: The Things You Normalize
text: I think the thing that sits with me most isn’t what happened. It’s what you’ve made normal for yourself without realizing it. The smoking. The vaping. The 2am guilt spirals that you turn outward instead of sitting with. The way you reach for something external every time something internal gets loud. I’m not saying that as a judgment. I’m saying it as someone who actually paid attention to you. Who watched your patterns because I was interested in the whole person, not just the version you present. I saw more than you probably wanted me to see.

title: The Idea I Had Of You
text: I had a version of you in my head that was genuinely beautiful. Not perfect, I wasn’t naive, but real and layered and worth the effort of knowing properly. Someone who could hold weight. Someone who understood that real things are quiet and slow and don’t need an audience. I was building toward that version of you. Slowly. In my own way. And then something happened and I had to update the file. Not delete it. Just update it. The original idea is still in there somewhere. I just can’t lead with it anymore.

title: I Can’t Figure You Out And I’ve Tried
text: I’ve run this back more than I want to admit. Looked at the whole sequence, tried to find the variable I was missing, the thing that would make it make sense. And I keep landing in the same place. Not anger. Just this honest, specific confusion that I don’t experience often. Because I loved you. I love you. In my own quiet way that doesn’t perform itself or ask for a witness. The kind that shows up in small decisions and middle of the night thoughts and voice notes I almost sent and didn’t. That kind. And I still can’t figure out how someone stands that close to something real and flinches. I’ve tried to understand it. I genuinely have. I just don’t.

title: The Door Is Still There
text: I’m still here. Just sit with that for a second without making it into something performative. I’m someone who has zero problem with distance, with closing things cleanly, with walking away from situations that cost more than they return. I’ve done it before without losing sleep. So the fact that I’m in this space still, that I chose to come back to it, that I’m writing any of this at all, that’s not nothing. It’s actually everything if you know how to read me. Don’t make it loud. Don’t make it a moment. Just understand what it means quietly. And walk through this carefully. That’s all I’m asking.

title: In Our Own Way
text: I don’t need you to understand all of this. Genuinely. I’m not writing it so you understand it, I’m writing it because it’s 2am and I had a good day, a genuinely good day, and my body is tired in the right way and my head is clear and somehow I’m still here. Putting words down. About you. Figure that out. I’m not asking you to out loud. Just. Notice it. In our own way, in the specific quiet language that we speak that doesn’t need an audience or a declaration, this is what it looks like when something actually meant something to me. That’s it. That’s the whole thing.
